description: What the suite of the lifecycle hooks on the real managers must notice: who ends with SubagentStop and who with Stop (a spawned agent, a second conversation a person started, a coding worker), a hook text that never reaches the model, a loop guard that lets one block too many through, and a block that touches the permission mode (the Read Only criterion).

mutations.name: M1
mutations.what: a spawned agent is not marked as a subagent: it ends with Stop

mutations.name: M2
mutations.what: every child runner is a subagent, also a second conversation a person started

mutations.name: M3
mutations.what: the roles are the wrong way round

mutations.name: M4
mutations.what: a coding worker is not marked as a subagent

mutations.name: M5
mutations.what: a coding worker has the wrong agent_type

mutations.name: M6
mutations.what: the identity is ignored when the loop asks

mutations.name: M7
mutations.what: a block also switches Read Only to Autonomous (the escalation the criterion forbids)

mutations.name: M8
mutations.what: a block also sets the execution policy to full-access

mutations.name: M9
mutations.what: one block too many is honored

mutations.name: M10
mutations.what: the hook's text never reaches the model
